maria_support: Hey team, spinning up a ticket — customers seeing streaming responses where older partial payloads arrive after newer ones on reconnects. Repro on TS SDK 1.7.2 and node16. Happens when token refresh + reconnect occurs (wallet service). Request ID: rwd-req-2026-06-12-1217. Model: llama-13b-q. Region: us-west-2. Symptoms: client iterates chunks A->B->C, then after reconnect we see C then (delayed) A',B' appended.

jonathan_engineer: Can you paste a minimal trace/log? Is this only when auth rotates or also intermittent disconnects?

maria_support: Minimal steps I gave to customer: 1) start streaming generation 2) force token rotate (simulated) 3) client reconnects using SDK auto-resume 4) observe late fragments. I have a small log excerpt: 
```
[12:17:01.123] evt seq=100 chunk: {"id":"A","text":"first"}
[12:17:02.200] evt seq=101 chunk: {"id":"B","text":"middle"}
[12:17:02.900] connection lost, reconnecting...
[12:17:03.050] new conn established
[12:17:03.100] evt seq=103 chunk: {"id":"C","text":"final"}
[12:17:03.250] delayed flush evt seq=100 chunk: {"id":"A","text":"first"}
[12:17:03.260] delayed flush evt seq=101 chunk: {"id":"B","text":"middle"}
```
Client code uses the TS SDK async iterator.

priya_sre: @maria_support thanks. Two quick theories: 1) upstream proxy (nginx/lb) buffered chunks and replayed them after the new conn; 2) SDK internal buffer flush code racing with reconnect path so old chunks are emitted after resume. Any flags about heartbeat/seqnums enabled?

maria_support: We saw heartbeat events every 2s. No explicit monotonic seq header from server (only per-event seq field in payload like above).

sam_sdk: I'm on it. Quick notes: TS SDK auto-resume merges buffered frames from previous EventSource stream into the resumed iterator queue. If the reconnect flow doesn't cancel the previous buffer flush timer it can append older buffered frames after the new stream starts. That matches your logs. Could also be exacerbated if client processes frames in a worker and flush order isn't gated by the server seq.

jonathan_engineer: Do we have any recent changes in the iterator implementation? IIRC we changed the backpressure microtask to improve latency in 1.7.0 — might have introduced a race.

sam_sdk: Yep, 1.7.0 changed how we schedule queued frame deliveries (moved to setImmediate-ish path). Reconnect cancels the EventSource but doesn't always clear the delivery queue on Node due to an edge with AbortController abort timing.

maria_support: Customer repro attached (gist link): https://gist.redwood/rwd-late-payload-repro — includes a small node script using eventsource + our SDK iterator. They see it on both local and kubernetes.

priya_sre: Operationally, I also pulled the LB logs — no replays detected on the load balancer side for those req ids. That makes SDK internal race much more likely.

sam_sdk: Short-term mitigation: recommend customer bump to SDK option {dropStaleOnResume: true} (we can enable this flag in vendor-backed SDK builds) — this will discard buffered frames with seq < resume_seq. Also set streamingHeartbeatIntervalMs to 1000 to detect disconnects quicker.

maria_support: I suggested the dropStaleOnResume workaround and they confirmed it reduces occurrences. They want a root-cause fix and a patch because they can't flip flags globally.

jonathan_engineer: Assigning to eng-runtime to verify server-side seq monotonicity and to SDK team for a fix. We'll need an integration test that force-rotates tokens mid-stream and asserts monotonic seq order delivered to iterator.

sam_sdk: Plan: 1) Add explicit resume_seq header emitted by server on resume handshake (helps server/sdks align), 2) Ensure iterator flush queue is fully drained/cancelled on reconnect before merging new stream, 3) Add e2e test in CI (Node + Browser). I'll open PR with changelog and propose hotfix 1.7.3.

dev-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1943 — affected SDKs: ts 1.7.2, py 0.9.8 (py may have related pattern), priority P2, assignee: sam_sdk. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1943

priya_sre: FYI adding feature request for server to emit monotonic frame seq in headers (x-rwd-frame-seq) in addition to payload seq — will make client-side dedupe easier for third-party SDKs.

maria_support: Customer was notified and accepted workaround. They're waiting for the hotfix and e2e test before we close. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam_sdk: I'll post the draft PR link soon and ping when a canary build is available for them to test.

jonathan_engineer: Marking this thread for follow-up in eng-releases once PR is merged.

maria_support: closing loop: customer verified canary: 1.7.3-canary.2 fixed ordering on their workload. Will roll to prod after GA. Thanks team! :party:
